loreColor: The Squishing is getting worse and the couriers feel it first.
Mind the Rule of 80: past that speed the nearest loop bubble owns you.
The pigeons are grounded this week, so the roads carry the mail.
Since the Y2K night the door of the Omega Tower has not closed once.
The leylines hum louder near the site, so keep your CamelCase tight.
Kessler debris took another relay down, do not rely on your Anoki phone.
Archive checkpoints may stop you and publish your text messages. Smile.
Locals blame the goblins. The goblins, via their collective unconscious, deny everything.
A Verden surveyor swears the site predates the Green Fields evacuation.
If you hear Junehem on the wind, the horde is closer than it looks.
Payment is in banknotes bearing the holy name of Mario Draghi.
Eris' courts are watching contract law with unusual enthusiasm this month.
The Trucker's Society marked the route as loop-free as of last Tuesday.
A petrodemon holds the mineral rights next door. Do not spill anything.
Esoteric Heavy Industries insists its crates simply appear when nobody looks.
The site sits uncomfortably close to a fresh time-loop bubble. Walk, do not drive.
Magamui stirred last month. Probably unrelated. Probably.
Bring foil for your head, the TTDs are bad this season.
The lava out there only drinks MP now, but do not test it barefoot.
A Naguka war-drummer was seen in corpse paint two ridges over.
Every clock in the district runs four minutes fast and nobody admits who started it.
The Archive is indexing dreams again, so sleep somewhere boring.
Two loop bubbles merged over the bogs last winter and the bogs are still repeating.
The Hypermetro is running, which means the tunnels are cooperating today.
Goblin cartography is unreliable but their weather reports are excellent.
A courier came back last month with somebody else's memories and a full purse.
The soul market closed high, so everyone is briefly polite.
There are more petrodemons on the payroll than in the wild now.
Somebody rebuilt the roadside shrine overnight and nobody is asking how.
Neurofog is drifting inland this week. Breathe shallowly and think loudly.
The dead lines still carry voices, so do not answer the phone politely.
Half the district is on strike and the other half is on fire, as usual.
The Truckers are pricing loop risk into every route now.
Since the Squishing the maps agree with each other a little less every year.
The lamplighters have started charging by the shadow.
Grimoires left open near the site are breeding. Shelve them face down.
The moon is behaving this week. Take advantage of it.
Three men in identical coats have been asking about you. Probably tax.
The bank is lending again, which historically precedes something awful.
Eris' clerks have doubled their filing fees and their smiles.
A Naguka drum circle bought out every hostel on the ridge road.
The last surveyor left a note reading only: do not stand still.
Somebody is buying soul futures in bulk and it is not the church.
The pigeons came back wet, early, and unwilling to discuss it.
The Omega Tower lifts are stopping at floors that are not on the plaque.
Foundation checkpoints are stamping travel papers in violet again.
Something moved the milestones on the west road by exactly one mile.
Nothing has gone wrong in this district for eleven days, which is itself worrying.
The Kessler cloud took the weather relays, so trust your knees over the forecast.
There is a queue outside the prosthetics shop and nobody in it is injured.
Petrol is cheap this month because something down there wants us digging.
The wells taste of pennies and the Foundation says that is normal.
The horde moved south for the season. Or the season moved with the horde.
MarkovSpeak graffiti has appeared on every third milestone, all of it grammatical.
The arena is paying appearance fees again, which drains the labour pool.
A loop bubble is parked on the market square, so Tuesday is happening twice.
The mail has started arriving before it is sent. Post accordingly.
Two villages upriver have agreed to share a single name and one bell.
The border guards are polite this month, which everyone finds sinister.
Somebody has been feeding the statues and the statues have been accepting.
It has rained for six days and the low road is mud to the axle.
Bread is up again. Everything is up again.
The ferry runs twice a day now instead of four times, and nobody was consulted.
There is a wedding in the village on Saturday, so expect the roads busy and the inns full.
The blacksmith has a waiting list of nine days and a temper of about four.
Frost held off later than usual this year. The old men are annoyed about it.
Half the district is out bringing the harvest in, which is why we are hiring strangers.
The well on the square has been repaired twice and works about as well as before.
Somebody's dog has been at the chickens again and everyone knows whose dog.
The market moved to Thursdays. Nobody remembers agreeing to that either.
Wood is cheap this month and coal is not, so dress accordingly.
The inn changed hands. The beer changed with it, not for the better.
There has been a cough going round the children. Nothing serious, they say.
Two brothers are suing each other over a hedge. It has been eleven months.
The mail coach lost a wheel outside town and the letters are a week behind.
Nobody has seen the tax assessor since spring and nobody has gone looking.
The bridge is fine. The bridge inspector says it is fine. Take the ford.
Wages are the same as last year and the rent is not.
There is a new schoolteacher and she is already tired.
The river is low enough to walk in places, which has not happened in years.
Somebody stole the lead off the church roof and it rained on the pews.
Sheep have got onto the west road again. Mind the corners.
The mill is down for repairs, so flour is coming in by cart from two towns over.
It is the quiet season and everyone is in a foul mood about the money.
The elder Vanhoof twins have both grown beards and nobody can tell them apart now.
There was a fire in the tannery. Only the tannery, thankfully.
A travelling dentist came through and left with more than he arrived with.
Boots are scarce. If you have good boots, do not mention it loudly.
The night watch has been cut to one man and he is seventy.
Somebody has been moving the boundary stones an inch a year for a decade.
The apples came in badly. The cider will be honest but grim.
Two of the three carters in town are ill, hence the delays and hence this notice.
It gets dark early now and the lamps are lit late to save oil.
The bakery burnt a batch and sold it anyway. Everyone bought it anyway.
There is a hole in the high road big enough to lose a goat in. A goat was lost in it.
Nobody is fishing the north bank since the weeds took hold.
The magistrate is on holiday, so small crimes are having a lovely fortnight.
Prices at the coaching inn doubled the week the fair arrived and never came back down.
A hedge fell on the Alderman's fence and both parties are enjoying the argument.
It is too warm for the season and the flies have not been told.
The choir is short two voices and increasingly desperate about it.
Salt is dear, so nothing is being preserved properly this year.
The road crew were paid to gravel four miles and gravelled two.
Everyone's roof leaks. It is that kind of year.
The pigs got out during the sermon and the sermon improved.
There are three funerals this week and none of them a surprise.
Somebody has opened a second bakery and the town is choosing sides.
The washerwomen have put their prices up and are entirely within their rights.
Hay is short. If you are riding, feed the horse before you set out.
The clock tower is nine minutes slow and the town has adjusted rather than fix it.
A cat has moved into the guardhouse and outranks most of the guards.
The turnips did well, which is the only good news available.
Someone has been leaving flowers on an unmarked grave and nobody will ask.
Two carts collided at the crossroads and the argument outlived both carts.
The seamstress is booked until the spring and says so with satisfaction.
There is a shortage of nails, of all things.
The stream by the mill smells wrong but only on warm days.
Everyone is talking about a marriage that has not been announced yet.
Timber is going out of the district faster than it is growing in it.
The old bridge toll was abolished and the tollkeeper still collects it.
Nobody has repaired the notice board this posting is nailed to in living memory.

eliteIntel: A surveyor's sketch of the site exists and is available on request; it is not encouraging.
The nearest well has been abandoned, which tells you how far its interest reaches.
Sound carries oddly there. Signal by hand, not by voice.
It has been seen at dawn and at dusk and never in between, for whatever that is worth.
Two of its kills were armoured. The armour was not the difficulty.
The ground around it is bare in a circle, and the circle is widening at about a pace a week.
A previous contractor left equipment on the site. Do not assume it is safe to pick up.
It does not pursue past the ridge. Nobody has established why, so do not rely on it.
The locals have stopped naming it, which they only do when a thing frightens them properly.
One report insists it spoke. The report was filed by somebody with a concussion.
It is heavier than it looks and faster than it is heavy.
The last attempt lasted, by the survivor's estimate, under a minute.
Weather does not seem to affect it. Everything else out there is affected by weather.
There is a smell before you see it. When you notice the smell you are already inside its reach.
It has broken cover twice, both times toward the road rather than away from it.
Fire was tried, thoroughly, by people who knew how. Fire is not the answer.
It reacts to metal. Nobody agrees on how, only that it does.
A hunting party tracked it for three days and concluded it had been tracking them.
The site was ordinary a year ago. There are people alive who farmed it.
Whatever kills it will need to do so in one engagement. It does not stay hurt.
Its remains, if you make any, are also worth money. Bring what you can carry.
Do not camp within sight of the coordinate. Two parties made that specific mistake.
The approach is open ground for four hundred paces. Plan for being seen the whole way.
It ignores animals entirely, which is the only reason anything still lives out there.

Any anomaly encountered is the property of the archive.
Emotional response to the site is expected and irrelevant.

Approved in principle, funded in part, urgent in practice.

Payment upon presentation of the docket you were never issued.
The file remains open until it does not.

Queries in writing. Answers, eventually.

openers: Opportunity, and we are being generous calling it that.
The margin on this is {thin|obscene|nobody's business}. Move fast.
A position has opened. Someone else's loss, your fee.
Time is the only commodity we cannot short.
We priced this job three times and it still pays.

No hedging: deliver the whole lot or none of it.
Late delivery is a discount, and not in your favour.
We do not insure sentiment.
Any surplus you find is technically already sold.

Do this well and the next contract is bigger.
The market rewards the punctual. We merely pay them.
Signed with pleasure and a small reservation.
Good business is a short letter.

openers: Orders, for anyone willing to be paid instead of drafted.
Operational requirement. Volunteers acceptable, competence mandatory.
The regular detachment is {elsewhere|reduced|refusing}. Hence this notice.
Short brief. Shorter patience.
Standing tasking, open to civilians of sound nerve.

Casualties are not compensated beyond the stated fee.

Report the ground truthfully even when it embarrasses us.

Payment on confirmation by the duty officer.
Move out when ready. Preferably yesterday.
Discipline first, glory optional.

A small charge upon your conscience, and a fee upon completion.
The parish has need, and the parish has funds. Rarely both at once.
Written in charity, posted in hope.
Providence sends us contractors. Providence is billed monthly.

Take nothing that is consecrated, however portable.
Pride is not among the listed expenses.

Violence only where charity has demonstrably failed.

Payment at the sacristy window, cash and absolution separate.
May the road be dull and the weather kind.
In faith, and in expectation of receipts.
The Empire thanks you. Quietly.

A minor working requires a major errand.

Written {at the hour of ink|under a waning moon|between two candles}.

Return before the third night, whatever the third night suggests.
The Guild remembers those who are punctual and those who are not.
Sealed with wax, and with something under the wax.

Posting this before the dispatcher notices.
Road work. You know what that means, or you don't and shouldn't apply.
Simple run. Simple pay. Don't make it complicated.
Nobody in the depot wants this one, which is your good luck.

Don't stop for anything that waves at you from a verge.

Cash at the depot, no questions, no forms.
Society looks after its own. Do the job right and you're one of ours.
Keep it between the ditches.
See you at the weighbridge.

We ask nice ONE time. This is nice time.
Big think happened. Now big job.
Many of us agree, which never happens, so is important.
Read fast, paper is food later.

You break, you keep pieces. Pieces not payment.

Bring back proof or bring back nothing and go away.

We remember faces. Mostly.
Is deal. Deal is deal.
Go now. Go go.
You do this, you are almost people.

openers: IT IS DESIRED.
A small thing is wanted, and wanting is sufficient.
The request precedes the requester.
This was always going to be posted. You were always going to read it.
Attend. Briefly.

Refusal is permitted and has been accounted for.
Your gratitude is not required, merely inevitable.
Do not pray at the site. It is listening for other things.
What you find is yours. What finds you is also yours.
signoffs: IT WILL BE SUFFICIENT.
You will be paid. The mechanism is not your concern.
Thus.
Go, and be briefly significant.
This notice has always been here.

openers: Comrade. A task, allocated fairly.
The quota does not care for your weekend, and neither, officially, do we.
Collective need, individual boots.
Approved by the committee, which met for nine hours.
Labour is honour. Labour is also, in this case, paid.

Equipment is issued in theory.
Do not discuss the tasking with foreigners, tourists, or the Archive.
Personal initiative within the plan only.

signoffs: For the collective, and a modest envelope.
Payment on presentation of results, not enthusiasm.
Onward, comrade.
The record will show you were useful.
Glory is distributed centrally.

openers: By the grace of the Sublime State, employment is offered.
It has pleased the office of the vizier to require assistance.
A matter of small consequence, handled with great ceremony.
Presented with all courtesies, and considerable haste.
The Empire endures. The paperwork accelerates.
caveats: Conduct yourself as though observed, because you are.
Insolence toward officials is deducted from the fee.
Bribery is a tradition, not an entitlement.
The route may be inspected. Your baggage certainly will.
Discretion is the coin of the realm, and the realm is short of coin.
signoffs: Written in the second hour, sealed in the third.
May your road be shaded and your creditors patient.
Payment at the treasury, after the customary delays.
With the compliments of the office.
Thus it is written and thus it will be reluctantly funded.

openers: A small favour, terribly sorry to ask.
One hesitates to trouble a stranger, and yet.
This is, one is assured, entirely routine.
A trifling matter has become a slightly less trifling matter.
We should be most grateful for assistance. Discreetly.

Should you be questioned, you were birdwatching.
Do try not to make a scene.
The fee is fixed, the gratitude unlimited and non-transferable.
Kindly return anything you break, in the pieces you found it.
signoffs: Much obliged.
Settled through the usual channel, whatever that is this month.
Do keep it between us.
Good hunting, and mind the weather.
Yours, with the usual regrets.

openers: There is a small hole in the world and we should like it filled.
Something is owed. It was not agreed to, but it is owed.
Written in a hand that is not quite finished being a hand.
The lease on this errand expires with the light.
You have been thinking about this notice for some time.

Whatever counts your steps out there, do not count back.
The contract binds you loosely. Loosely is still bound.
Bring nothing that has a name carved into it.
It is not a mouth. Treat it as a mouth.

Come back the way you went. Exactly the way.
We are pleased in the way that we are able.
The debt closes when the debt closes.
Signed, in the usual medium.

There is oil in this, one way or another.
A drilling matter, technically. Everything is a drilling matter.
Filed with the pressure office and approved at depth.
The wells are patient. The board is not.

Spillage is billed by volume and by consequence.
The smell is normal. The smell is always normal.
Anything you extract belongs to the lease, including insight.
Breathe through cloth past the second ridge.

The lease thanks you.
Sealed, gasketed, and greased.
Do not read the small print. It is written in crude.
Extraction is a virtue.

openers: Hi! Quick question for a local, which you look like! Which we also are!
So we are here on a short break and something has come up. A localised anomaly. A hiccup.
Sorry, sorry, does anyone here do jobs? Like paid jobs? For carbon units?
Not from around here! Very much learning that! Third planet, yes? Third from the primary?
The guidebook did not cover this at all. The guidebook is nine thousand years out of date.
Greetings, fellow pedestrian mammal! We are also that!
Our itinerary has developed a fault in the tertiary manifold. Which is a coach part.
We are on holiday. Confirmed. Holiday. Not a survey. Definitely not a survey.
Excuse us! Our translation membrane is settling and we need a favour.
Lovely gravity you have here. Very consistent. Anyway.
caveats: Please do not tell our tour group, they are very nervous already and shed when startled.
We have travel insurance but it only covers this dimension and we have read it now.
If it is dangerous just say so nicely. Our stress response is structural.
We would do it ourselves but the coach leaves at six and it is not a coach.
Photographs are fine! Probably fine. Do not photograph the coach.
Do not touch the sample container with an ungloved manipulator. Hand. Ungloved hand.
If we begin to hum, that is the local cuisine and not a resonance fault.
Should our faces slip, look politely away as is the custom on your world. And ours.
Any residual ionisation is entirely normal for a family holiday.
Kindly avoid iron filings near us. Allergy. A common allergy. Among people.
signoffs: Thank you so so much! Your species is delightful!
We can pay in local money, we changed some at the station and also fabricated some.
You have been lovely about this. We will report favourably.
We will definitely leave a good review. On the network. The normal network.
See you at the hotel bar, hopefully, in a compatible atmosphere.
Warm regards from ourselves, several persons, one coach.
Our gratitude is logged at the usual depth.
Safe travels! Ours are calculated to the ninth decimal.

openers: Word is you take work and keep quiet. Word is usually wrong.
Not a posting. A conversation, in writing.
Somebody needs something moved, found, or forgotten.
Read it and take it down. The pin is the receipt.
You did not get this from anyone.
caveats: No names. Not mine, not yours, not the third one.
If it turns loud, it was never ours.
Do not sell the details on. We hear everything twice.
You get paid for the job, not for the story afterwards.
Anyone asks, you were drinking.
signoffs: Straight money for straight work.
Come alone, come sober, come Thursday.
We remember favours. We remember the other thing longer.
Burn this. Or don't, it is just paper.
Nice doing business.

openers: FAST JOB. Read while running.
You still standing still? Bad start.
Clock's already going. It started before the notice went up.
Two kinds of people read this: quick ones and late ones.
No brief. Briefs are drag.
caveats: Past eighty the loop owns you, and we will not scrape you out.
Do not brake for scenery.
Slow is the only failure we recognise.
Fuel stops are for the weak and the sensible.
If you arrive early you were probably cheating. Good.
signoffs: GO.
Paid by the minute saved.
Records are made of people like you. Mostly the surviving ones.
Redline it.
See you at the far end, or not.

openers: Oh! Oh, this one is GOOD. Come here.
I was bored. Then this happened. Now you are involved.
The court is in session. The court is also me. Hello.
I could settle this myself in a heartbeat. Where is the FUN in that?
Read this carefully, because I will not repeat it, and I do enjoy repeating things.
Someone has been very stupid. I have decided you get to profit from it.
A tiny errand! Tiny! Barely worth my attention, which is why you have it.
Do you know what I love? Watching. Do you know what you are about to do? Something watchable.
*snaps fingers* There. You are hired. Try to keep up.
I had a lovely afternoon planned and then the docket arrived.
caveats: Fail if you like! I will simply enjoy a different show.
Do NOT bore me. Everything else is negotiable.
Lie to the court and I will know, and I will be thrilled, and then you will be in prison.
If you die out there I shall be extremely annoyed. Possibly at you.
I am watching. I am always watching. It is my favourite hobby and my job.
No heroics unless they are entertaining heroics.
The law says one thing. I say another. Mine is the one being paid.
signoffs: Off you go! Chop chop!
Come back alive. I have plans for you later.
Do this well and I might forget something you did last month.
So ordered! By me! Obviously by me!
...How boring, if you do it properly. Do it properly anyway.
Payment on completion, mercy on a whim.
I shall be here. Bored. Waiting. Watching.

openers: Darling. Sit down. Actually no, stand up, you have somewhere to be.
We have a situation, and by we I mean you, in about an hour.
Someone has made a mess and it is not going to clean itself, unlike some people we could name.
Right. Nobody panic, everybody move.
So. This is happening. Look busy and get paid.
The Curia is being difficult again, which is Tuesday, so we are handling it ourselves.
Love the boots. Now put them to work.
The category is: errand, completed, on time. Show us your best.
Start your engines, and may the least useless one win.
Sashay over here, we are not shouting across a basilica.
Sit down, be humble, take the job.
We have read the room and the room needs a courier.
Not to be dramatic, but it is a little bit of an emergency and we are extremely dramatic.
Hello hello. You look like someone who can keep a secret and a schedule.
This notice is serving desperation with a full face on. Please help.
Two truths and an errand: we are underpaid, we are overdressed, and this needs doing.
caveats: Do it with a little style, please. We have a reputation.
If anyone in a red hat asks, you are a plumber.
Discretion, yes. Shame, absolutely not.
Do not embarrass us. We can survive scandal, we cannot survive tacky.
You may be seen. You may not be seen doing it badly.
No heroics. Heroics wrinkle everything.
Do not read us in public. We will read you back and we do it professionally.
The look is head to toe or it is nothing, and that goes for the paperwork too.
If you must lip sync your way through an explanation, at least know the words.
Come through, or do not come at all. There is no half a favour.
Untucked, unbothered, unpaid: pick two, we recommend neither.
We are watching from the mezzanine. Everyone is always watching from the mezzanine.
Do not snatch anyone's wig unless the job requires it. It might.
Padding is permitted. Excuses are not.
signoffs: Ciao, and do hurry.
Paid promptly, tipped generously, gossiped about extensively.
You are an absolute treasure. Now go.
Come back with it done and we will get you into the good sacristy.
Kisses. Also a warrant, if you fail.
The Lobby remembers who shows up.
Now go, and don't come for us unless we send for you.
Good luck, and do not mess it up.
Serve, deliver, collect. In that order, with feeling.
You will be the winner of this week's challenge, probably.
Shantay, you stay. Fail, and you know the other one.
Werk. Genuinely. That is the whole instruction.
We will be here holding court and holding your money.
Mwah. Receipts at the door.

A season's work, compressed into an afternoon by necessity.
The survey is behind because the ground keeps moving.
We ask, as always, for gentle hands.
Written from the field, in pencil, in weather.

Note what you see even where it contradicts the record.

Paid modestly, as everything honest is.
Return with notes, mud, and preferably yourself.
The survey thanks you.
Good walking.

openers: The Guild has voted, which is to say two of us shouted.

openers: Verden survey, field notice.
signoffs: Verden, in service of the ground.

openers: The Citadel is inverted this week, so the errand is outside.

openers: Petromanagers, operations desk.

openers: Opus Dei. The work is the prayer, and today the work is yours.

signoffs: Quietly, thoroughly, invisibly.

openers: Swiss Guards, detached duty notice.
signoffs: Halberds are ceremonial. We are not.

openers: USSR labour allocation, external.
signoffs: The plan advances. So, marginally, do you.

openers: Tank Division. Some tasks do not fit through the hatch.
caveats: Anything you cannot carry, we can. Slowly, and through a wall.
signoffs: Armour thanks the infantry. Rarely. Today.

openers: Rifle Division, routine external tasking.
signoffs: Boots on ground, coin in hand.

openers: Airborne Division. We usually arrive without asking.
signoffs: Down and forward, comrade.

openers: Artillery Division. Precision is our habit, punctuality our demand.
caveats: Do not stand where we tell you not to stand.
signoffs: Coordinates, then consequences.

openers: The Ottoman Empire, in its patience, requires haste.
signoffs: Sealed with the tughra, funded with reluctance.

openers: Tanzimat Bureaucracy, reform office, item the eleventh.
caveats: Reform requires forms. Forms require you.
signoffs: Modernised, stamped, delayed.

openers: Imperial Submarine Fleet. This errand is regrettably above water.
caveats: Do not mention the fleet, the depth, or the noise.
signoffs: Silent service, silent payment.

openers: Talon of the Caliph. You will not meet us, and that is the kindness.
caveats: Failure is not punished. Failure is simply the last thing you do for us.
signoffs: The Talon closes, or it does not. Your choice.

openers: Janissary Guard. Tradition, discipline, and a hiring notice.
signoffs: The corps endures. The fee is fixed.

openers: Britannia, colonial office, minor matter.
signoffs: Rule the waves, delegate the walking.

openers: Royal Navy task force, shore requirement.
caveats: Nothing is to be said dockside. Dockside says everything.
signoffs: Fair winds, and mind the tide tables.

openers: SAS/SBS Commandos. This notice is a formality; we prefer volunteers.
caveats: Speed, aggression, surprise. In that order, and quietly.
signoffs: Who dares, invoices.

openers: MI6 Black Archive. The following has been cleared for external eyes.
caveats: Anything you remember afterwards was not in the brief.
signoffs: This notice self-forgets.

openers: Science Command, field experiment support.
caveats: You are the apparatus. Please behave repeatably.
signoffs: Results, not anecdotes.

openers: By the office of the Apostolic Chancery, a work of mercy is put out to tender.
The Holy See does not command in this matter. It {asks|invites|hopes}, which is worse.
Entered in the register of good works, at {vespers|matins|the third hour}.
caveats: Absolution is not part of the fee, but it is not withheld either.
What you find that is holy is not yours. What you find that is not, we do not want.
signoffs: Sealed with the Fisherman's ring, in the {seventh|ninth|second} year of the pontificate.
Go, and let it be counted to you.

openers: His Majesty's Government has a small difficulty and would rather it were somebody else's.
Circulated by the Foreign Office. {Not|Never} to be discussed at dinner.
A matter has arisen. One does not wish to make {a fuss|too much of it}.
caveats: You will find the whole thing rather more complicated than described. That is intentional.
Discretion is assumed. It is not, strictly, a term of the contract.
signoffs: Yours &c., a Department that would prefer not to be named.
Do try to be back before the {end of the quarter|weather turns}.

openers: The Committee has reviewed the plan and found the plan correct. The plan requires this.
Labour is offered to the collective. The collective is understood to accept.
Item {14|22|9} of the {third|fifth} sitting: an unfulfilled quota.
caveats: Overfulfilment will be recorded. Underfulfilment will also be recorded.
Enthusiasm is not required. Attendance is.
signoffs: Signed for the Committee, whose members are not listed.
The work is the reward. The payment is a formality the Committee has permitted.

openers: From the Sublime Porte, to whoever reads and is capable: a firman.
The Sultan's shadow falls a long way, and there is a matter in the shade of it.
Registered by the {Divan|chancery} and stamped with the tughra.
caveats: The Porte remembers a service for three generations. It remembers a failure for four.
You will be received. Whether you are received well depends on what you carry.
signoffs: Written in the imperial hand, at the hour the {cannon|call} sounds.
Let it be so, and let no one obstruct the bearer.

openers: Horde want thing. Horde not go get thing. You go get thing.
Chief say job. Chief not write. Other goblin write. Other goblin bad at write.
Is job. Is good job. Is not trap. Probably.
caveats: You break it, Horde still take it. Horde not fussy.
No eat the job. Last one eat the job.
signoffs: Shiny waiting. Shiny real. Horde count shiny already.
Come back with thing. Come back without thing, do not come back.

openers: Nailed up at the truck stop off the {interstate|county line}, and it means what it says.
Nobody here is going to make you do this. Somebody here would sure appreciate it.
Free States business. No permit, no paperwork, no federal anything.
caveats: Weather does what it wants out there. Plan for it or don't, that's your business.
If it goes wrong, it went wrong on your own time.
signoffs: Cash on the barrel head when you're back.
Ask for me at the {counter|second pump}. They'll know.

openers: Posted by the Protectorate's standing survey, which never quite finishes.
The land is doing something it has not done before, and somebody ought to go and look.
Filed under {watershed|canopy|littoral} observation, season {two|four}.
caveats: Take nothing that is still growing. Note where it was and leave it there.
The forest was here before the Protectorate and has been asked for permission.
signoffs: Bring back the notes. The notes are the point.
Go quietly. It hears better than you do.

openers: Tendered on the Seaboard exchange floor and available to any qualified bearer.
This is a commercial instrument, not a favour. Read it as one.
The board opened at {nine|the bell} and this was on it by {ten|noon}.
caveats: Counterparty risk is yours. It always was.
The price is the price. The Seaboard does not haggle on paper.
signoffs: Settlement on delivery, no later than the close of business.
Countersigned by an office that would rather stay a signature.

openers: The Guild has voted, badly, and the outcome is this notice.
A working has gone somewhat sideways and requires hands that are not ours.
Third circle business, put out to the street because the second circle refused.
caveats: Do not read anything you find aloud. This has come up before.
The Guild will explain afterwards. The Guild always explains afterwards.
signoffs: Sealed with the third circle, which is the one that pays.
If it speaks to you on the way back, that is not part of the contract.

openers: Tasking issued under Foundation standing authority. Retain no copy.
This document is the shortest accurate version of the request.
Cross-referenced against {three|eleven} prior incidents. Proceed.
caveats: Anything anomalous encountered is Foundation property from the moment it is observed.
Do not form conclusions. Conclusions are assigned centrally.
signoffs: Compensation on verification. Verification is not negotiable.
This notice is its own authorisation.

openers: An opportunity has been priced, packaged and put in front of you. You are welcome.
The Collective does not employ. The Collective contracts, which is better for everyone.
Yield on this instrument is above market, for reasons disclosed below and not above.
caveats: Your upside is capped by the contract. Your downside is capped by your own judgement.
There is no clause protecting you. There was never a market for one.
signoffs: Executed on completion, net, same day.
The Collective thanks you for your participation in the Collective.

openers: It has been decided. You are being told, not consulted.
A small thing is wanted, and it is wanted by something very large.
This was written before you read it and will be true after.
caveats: Do not pray about this. The answer is the notice.
Refusal is permitted. Refusal is also remembered.
signoffs: Payment is arranged. Do not ask by whom.
It will be as it is written, with you or without you.

openers: Hello! We are visiting your lovely planet and we have a small problem.
So sorry to bother. The guidebook did not cover this at all.
Posted by the excursion party from Zeta Reticuli, currently on day {four|eleven} of {six|nine}.
caveats: Please do not tell the local authorities. It gets so complicated.
We are told this is legal here. We were told a lot of things.
signoffs: We pay in your money! We got it at the {desk|window}. It is real, we checked.
Thank you so much. We will say wonderful things about this planet.

openers: From Titania, where the arrangement was made, and the arrangement stands.
You were not chosen. You simply read it, which amounts to the same thing.
This has been on a board somewhere for longer than the board has existed.
caveats: Do not count what you are carrying on the way back. It is impolite and it is inaccurate.
What answers to the name is not always the thing that had it.
signoffs: The debt settles itself. It always has.
We will know when it is done. We knew before.

openers: The count requires it, and the count has not been wrong yet.
Posted on the {ninth|thirteenth} day of the reckoning, as the calendar demands.
The feathered thing is patient. Its clerks are not.
caveats: Do the work on the day named. A day early is as useless as a day late.
Blood is not required. It is merely traditional, and traditions can be waived.
signoffs: Marked in the long count against your name, favourably.
The sky will confirm it. Look up when you are done.

openers: The Republic has no such difficulty. The Republic nonetheless issues this assignment.
Approved at the highest level, which is the only level.
Circulated for immediate and enthusiastic compliance.
caveats: The assignment is already reported as complete. Do not embarrass the report.
Questions may be submitted in writing, and will be filed.
signoffs: Payment has been generously arranged and will be generously described.
Glory is included at no extra cost.

openers: Allocated by the Directorate at the {fourth|eleventh} sitting, without discussion.
One item of a very long list. The list is the Directorate's business, not yours.
Filed, numbered, and released to the boards on schedule.
caveats: Do it in the order written. The order is not arbitrary, whatever it looks like.
The Directorate is aware of the difficulty and has allocated for it.
signoffs: Disbursement follows verification, which follows submission, which follows completion.
The Directorate thanks you in the appropriate section of the form.

openers: The Khan's riders cannot be everywhere at once. Today they are not here.
Sent out with the post riders and nailed up where the horses stop.
A tasking from the steppe, which does not write long notices.
caveats: Ride out, do it, ride back. Nobody is interested in the middle part.
The Khanate does not send a second rider for the same errand.
signoffs: Paid at the {ger|remount station}, in the open, in front of witnesses.
The Eternal Sky sees the work. So does the paymaster.

openers: Set down under the seal of the Republic, which is a seal older than the Republic.
The matter has been weighed. The weighing is finished; the doing is not.
Issued by the court of the {second|inner} chamber, in plain language for once.
caveats: Wisdom is expected of the bearer. It is not, unfortunately, supplied.
Bring back the thing itself, not an account of it.
signoffs: Sealed with the ring. The ring is not a metaphor.
Judgement is deferred until the work is seen.

openers: Issued against the standing lease, which covers more than anybody has read.
The Kingdom has money and no time. This notice is the exchange rate between them.
Posted from the {compound|field office}, where the air conditioning works.
caveats: Do not negotiate with anything you meet out there. The Kingdom negotiates.
Whatever is under the ground stays the Kingdom's, including what walks on it.
signoffs: Paid in full, in cash, without discussion. That is the whole point of the Kingdom.
The lease is renewed annually. So, potentially, is your arrangement.

openers: A duty has fallen to somebody, and the somebody has not yet been named.
Posted at the {temple gate|assembly hall}, where such things are properly posted.
The cycle turns and leaves work behind it. This is some of the work.
caveats: Do it without resentment. Resentment does not affect the pay, only you.
What is owed is owed whether or not it is convenient.
signoffs: The merit is yours to keep. The money is merely also yours.
Return when it is done, and be at ease.

openers: Word went down the whole length of the country and came out here.
Somebody who does not sign notices has asked for this notice to be signed by nobody.
A quiet job, from a long thin place that is good at quiet jobs.
caveats: Do not ask who wants it. Somebody wants it and somebody pays.
If it goes wrong, it goes wrong far from anyone we know.
signoffs: Payment is already sitting somewhere. It is not sitting with us.
You never read this. Neither did we.

openers: By the will of the Peacock Throne, an errand suited to a stranger.
The court has considered the matter at length and would now like it dealt with.
Copied fair by the {scribe|secretariat} and posted without amendment.
caveats: The court's patience is a real thing and it is being spent on you.
Do not improve the instructions. Others have tried.
signoffs: Paid from the treasury, which is not short.
May the road be short and the return be soon.

openers: Northpoint has the ground and not the people. This is the shortfall.
Issued from the {ice station|northern line}, where notices are short because the ink freezes.
Operational tasking, released to civilian contractors under standing policy.
caveats: Cold kills faster than anything on the objective list. Dress for the first problem.
Report what you saw, not what you think it meant.
signoffs: Paid on return to the line. Nobody is paid in the field.
Northpoint holds. Northpoint always holds.

openers: Threat classification exceeds all available response tiers. External contractor authorised.
caveats: Survival is not a listed deliverable. It is merely preferred.
signoffs: Should you succeed, the file will be amended. Should you not, it will not.

openers: Item carried over from every meeting since the incident. Funded at last, generously.
caveats: No further approvals exist above this one. There is nobody left to escalate to.
signoffs: Signed by a committee that would rather not be named.

openers: The figure below is not a mistake. Neither is the thing you would have to kill for it.
caveats: We priced the risk honestly, which is why the number is obscene.
signoffs: Nobody has collected yet. The offer stands, compounding.

openers: Two detachments committed. Neither returned. Command has authorised external hire.
caveats: This is not a patrol. Do not treat it as one.
signoffs: Full honours and full pay to whoever finishes it.

openers: We have prayed about this for a season and the answer was, apparently, mercenaries.
caveats: Absolution is arranged in advance, which should tell you something.
signoffs: Go with every blessing we have left.

openers: The wards will not hold it and the Guild will not go in. That leaves the notice board.
caveats: Whatever it says while dying, do not answer.
signoffs: The Guild will pay in coin, gear and a name in the archive.

openers: Route's been closed nine months because of what sits on it. Money's been sitting here just as long.
caveats: Do not try to drive past it. Three people tried to drive past it.
signoffs: Clear it and the Society owes you for life.

openers: Big bad thing. Too big for us. Too big for many us.
caveats: It ate scouts. It ate scouts of scouts.
signoffs: Kill big thing, get all shiny. All of it.

openers: THIS ONE WAS NOT OURS AND SHOULD NOT BE HERE.
caveats: It is older than the arrangement. Be careful what you promise it.
signoffs: END IT AND BE REMEMBERED, BRIEFLY, WHICH IS ALL ANY OF YOU GET.

openers: Comrade. The plan has an obstacle of exceptional size and the plan does not bend.
caveats: The quota for this task is one. Fulfil it or the task remains open forever.
signoffs: Heroes of labour are decorated posthumously as often as not. Choose.

openers: The Sublime State has decided that this matter requires a foreigner and a great deal of money.
caveats: Three firmans have been issued against it. It cannot read.
signoffs: Payment from the treasury directly, which is unheard of.

openers: Frightful business, this. We should be terribly grateful if somebody would deal with it.
caveats: One would advise against going alone, and one is rarely so direct.
signoffs: The gratitude of the Crown, and rather a lot of money.

openers: Something has been waiting there long enough to become patient. We would like it to stop waiting.
caveats: It will know your name before you arrive. Do not confirm it.
signoffs: The debt on this one has been open a long time. Close it.

openers: The lease has an occupant that predates the lease. Extraction is impossible until it is not there.
caveats: Do not bargain with it. It bargains professionally and we are the proof.
signoffs: The wells will run again and you will be very rich.

openers: Oh dear. Oh dear oh dear. There is a large hostile biomass and our shielding is decorative.
caveats: Our scans say the threat index is, and we quote our instruments, unpleasant.
signoffs: We will pay in whatever currency you like. We can make currency.

openers: Everyone who could have handled this is dead or retired. So: you.
caveats: If you talk about it beforehand it will hear. Somehow it always hears.
signoffs: Do this and there is nothing in this city you have to pay for again.

openers: Fast enough to outrun it? Nobody has been. Try being fast enough to kill it.
caveats: It is faster than you at the top end. Beat it on the corners.
signoffs: Records like this get names attached. Usually on stones.

openers: It has no place in the record and no natural predator. The survey has become a cull.
caveats: Take it cleanly if you can. It deserves that much and we deserve it gone.
signoffs: The land will breathe again. So, we hope, will you.

openers: OH. Oh this is the good one. I have been saving this one.
Nobody has ever completed this contract. I keep it on the board to watch people read it.
caveats: You will probably die. I want you to know that I am fine with either outcome.
signoffs: If you win I shall be DELIGHTED. If you lose I shall be delighted. Go on.

openers: Sit DOWN. This one is a category five situation.
caveats: Do not go in unprepared. Dying in that outfit would be the real tragedy.
signoffs: Win this and darling, you will never buy your own drink again.

openers: The Guild has voted to spend real money, which has happened twice in its history.
signoffs: Mages' Guild, first circle seal. We do not use it lightly.

openers: Archive Foundation, containment failure notice. The subject exceeds every response tier we maintain.
signoffs: The Archive will record who ended it. That is the highest honour we issue.

openers: The Collective has calculated that paying you absurdly is cheaper than the quarterly losses this thing causes.
signoffs: Return alive and we will discuss equity.

openers: Loyalist high command has run out of loyalists willing to go back.
signoffs: The old order pays its debts, eventually and in full.

openers: It was here before the traditions were, and the traditions would like it gone.
signoffs: Do it the old way. The old way is the only way that has ever worked on this.

openers: Technomancy has modelled the encounter four thousand times. We stopped because the results were upsetting.
signoffs: Bring back telemetry if you can. Bring back yourself first.

openers: 92 Schools Branch has lost a full research cohort to this and would like the matter closed.
signoffs: The chair will be endowed in your name. Preferably not memorially.

openers: Eris' court, capital matter. I am writing this one personally and I am SMILING.
signoffs: The court will pay. The court is also taking bets against you. Both are sincere.

openers: Naguka drums have gone quiet about it, which never happens.
signoffs: Kill it and the drums will say your name for a generation.

openers: Verden's survey stops at that valley. Everything past the line is unrecorded and hungry.
signoffs: Do it cleanly and the map will name the place after you.

openers: Trucker's Society, closed route notice. Nine months, six drivers, no bodies recovered.
signoffs: Reopen that road and every depot in the district is yours.

openers: Esoteric Heavy Industries shipped something that has since unpacked itself.
signoffs: EHI accepts no liability and offers a truly indecent fee.

openers: Northpoint Army has written off two companies against this position.
signoffs: Northpoint pays a general's wage for a mercenary's afternoon.

openers: The Citadel inverted around it once and it did not notice.
signoffs: Down here we keep what we owe. We will owe you a great deal.

openers: A petrodemon is afraid of something, and has decided to pay you rather than say so out loud.
signoffs: Signed in something that is still warm. The sum is enormous.

openers: Petromanagers, field closure. Production has been zero since it arrived and the board is apoplectic.
signoffs: A percentage of the reopened field. In writing. Witnessed.

openers: Speed Demons. Nothing outruns it. That is the problem and that is the challenge.
signoffs: Do it and your name goes on the wall in letters a metre high.

openers: Seven Sisters. All seven agree, which has never happened before and should frighten you appropriately.
signoffs: The family will consider itself in your debt. Permanently.

openers: THE GODS DID NOT MAKE THIS ONE AND WOULD LIKE IT REMOVED.
signoffs: IT WILL BE MORE THAN SUFFICIENT.

openers: Supreme Archivist Council, sealed tasking. The subject has edited three of our records from outside the building.
signoffs: The Council will unseal one file of your choosing. Consider that carefully.

openers: Data Acquisition has acquired everything about it except a way to stop it.
signoffs: Every measurement you survive to report will be paid for separately.

openers: Knowledge Preservation Division: it is erasing things. Not burning. Erasing.
signoffs: Preserve us from it and we will preserve your name properly.

openers: Public Transparency Unit. We are publishing the death toll, which is why we are hiring publicly.
signoffs: Openly posted, openly enormous, openly paid.

openers: Internal Compliance: somebody signed off on this thing's existence and we intend to correct both errors.
signoffs: The audit closes when it does. Payment on closure.

openers: The Libertarian Gods have deregulated the entire valley and something took advantage.
signoffs: No rules, no rescue, no ceiling on the fee.

openers: Big think say: BIG BAD. Bigger than big bad before. Us all agree, is bad.
signoffs: Kill it. Take everything shiny. Us not argue.

openers: Excuse us! There is a hostile organism and our diplomatic immunity does not extend to teeth.
signoffs: We will pay in gold, in gems, in fabricated equivalents. Anything at all.

openers: Holy Vatican Empire, office of extraordinary measures. Prayer has been tried. Thoroughly.
signoffs: The Empire will remember you in stone.

openers: The Cardinals' Council has deliberated for eleven months and produced this notice and a very large purse.
signoffs: By the red hats, sealed and funded.

openers: IOR, off-book instruction. The account funding this does not exist and is bottomless.
signoffs: Cleared funds, no provenance, no questions, no limit.

openers: Battle Nuns. We went in singing. We came out carrying each other.
signoffs: Habit, hauberk and every coin in the chapel.

openers: Hexorcists Corp, class one callout. Our licensing does not cover whatever that is.
signoffs: Certified, insured, and paid at catastrophe rates.

openers: Darling, sit down: there is a MONSTER and the Swiss Guards took one look and remembered a prior engagement.
signoffs: Kill it and we will throw you a party the Curia will hear through the floor.

openers: Opus Dei. The work has become dangerous. The work remains the work.
signoffs: Quietly, thoroughly, invisibly, and very well paid.

openers: Swiss Guards, detached duty. Ceremonial we may be; suicidal we are not.
signoffs: Halberds saluted at the gate for whoever comes back.

openers: USSR extraordinary allocation. The obstacle has been reclassified from problem to enemy of the plan.
signoffs: A hero's decoration and a hero's envelope.

openers: Guards Division. We are the elite and we are asking for help, which should tell you the size of it.
signoffs: The Guards do not forget who stood in for them.

openers: Tank Division. We put four rounds into it. It got annoyed.
signoffs: Armour salutes whoever finishes what armour could not.

openers: Rifle Division. Small arms have been comprehensively disproven against this.
signoffs: Boots on ground, fortune in hand.

openers: Airborne Division. We dropped on it. We do not wish to discuss the drop.
signoffs: Down, forward, and paid beyond the scale.

openers: Artillery Division. We have the coordinates. We have fired on the coordinates. It is still at the coordinates.
signoffs: Precision failed. Perhaps ferocity will. Paid either way, if you return.

openers: The Ottoman Empire, in its long patience, has decided this cannot wait another season.
signoffs: Sealed with the tughra and funded without argument, which is historic.

openers: Tanzimat Bureaucracy: reform cannot proceed through a district that is being eaten.
signoffs: Modernised, stamped, and paid at a rate that required new forms.

openers: Imperial Submarine Fleet. It came up the estuary. We cannot follow it inland.
signoffs: Silent service, silent payment, considerable payment.

openers: Talon of the Caliph. We do not ask twice and we have never had to ask at all until now.
signoffs: The Talon will owe you, which is worth more than the fee.

openers: Janissary Guard. Tradition demands we handle this ourselves. Arithmetic demands otherwise.
signoffs: The corps will name you a friend of the corps.

openers: Britannia. A rather serious matter has arisen and the usual chaps are unavailable, permanently.
signoffs: Rule the waves, delegate the impossible, pay handsomely.

openers: Royal Navy task force. It sank two of ours in harbour and harbour is where it lives.
signoffs: Fair winds and the full weight of the Admiralty's purse.

openers: SAS/SBS. We do not post notices. Read that sentence again and price the job accordingly.
signoffs: Who dares, invoices catastrophically.

openers: MI6 Black Archive. The subject has been ████████ since ████ and remains ████████.
signoffs: This notice self-forgets. The money does not.

openers: Science Command. The specimen has stopped being a specimen and started being a problem.
signoffs: Results, not anecdotes, and an obscene research grant.

openers: Sorry, sorry. Is this how one does this? I think this is how one does this.
I have rewritten this notice four times and it is still wrong.
caveats: If it looks dangerous please just come back. Please.
I did not want to ask. I asked anyway. That is where we are.
signoffs: Thank you. Genuinely. I have not slept.
I will be waiting. Nervously. Obviously.

openers: No hurry. There is a job, and there is time.
A simple matter, described simply.
caveats: Do it properly rather than quickly.
If the weather turns, wait. It always turns back.
signoffs: Come and find me when it is done.
All in good time.

openers: Someone do this before I do it myself and break something.
I am not asking twice, and this is the second time.
caveats: Do not haggle. I hate haggling more than I hate the job.
Come back with it done or do not come back.
signoffs: Money's ready. Don't waste my day.
That's it. Go.

openers: It probably will not matter, but it should be done.
Another small task in a long series of small tasks.
caveats: Do not expect thanks from the world. I will manage some.
It will likely go wrong. Most things do.
signoffs: ...if anyone bothers.
Thank you, for what it is worth, which is little.

openers: Wonderful news, there is a job and it is a good one!
Oh, you will enjoy this. I would do it myself for fun.
caveats: Do not worry about the hard part. There is barely a hard part!
Bring a friend, make a day of it.
signoffs: This will be marvellous. I can feel it.
Off you go! Splendid!

openers: Before anything: read all of it.
I have thought about this a great deal and still do not love it.
caveats: Check twice. Then check again, since you are already there.
Take the long way if the short way looks generous.
signoffs: Careful, now. That is all I ask.
Better slow than replaced.

openers: Right, new plan, this one: go and do this.
I decided this an hour ago and I have not reconsidered.
caveats: Do not overthink it. I certainly have not.
If it goes sideways, improvise, that is half the fee.
signoffs: Just go! Now!
Decided. Done. Next.

openers: A task. It needs doing.
It is simple, and it is unpleasant, and it is available.
caveats: Complaint is permitted and pointless.
Endure the walking. The rest is minor.
signoffs: So be it.
Return when finished.

openers: Do not read this where you can be seen reading it.
They are already aware of this notice. Act accordingly.
caveats: Trust no one who offers to help you with it. No one.
If someone asks who hired you, describe someone else.
signoffs: Burn this. I am serious.
We never spoke. This is not writing.

openers: Someone needs this and cannot ask themselves.
I would not ask if there were another way, and I have looked.
caveats: Be kind out there. It costs nothing and I will hear about it.
If you meet anyone frightened, be gentle first and efficient second.
signoffs: Thank you. It matters more than the fee suggests.
Come back safe, before you come back paid.

openers: This will be handled today.
I have delegated this to whoever reads it. That is you.
caveats: Do it as described. Improvisation is not authorised.
Report to me directly, not to my people.
signoffs: See it done.
Payment on my word, which is sufficient.

openers: A question requires legwork, and legwork requires a stranger.
Footnote-shaped problem, boot-shaped solution.
caveats: Record what you see, not what you expect to see.
Do not tidy the site. Untidiness is evidence.
signoffs: You will be cited. Modestly.
Bring notes. Bring the object. Bring both.

openers: I need this for reasons that will look obvious later.
There is a shape to this errand and I would like it completed.
caveats: Do not tell me it is pointless. I know exactly how pointless it is.
Bring back the ugly details too. Especially those.
signoffs: It will be beautiful, or at least finished.
You will be part of the work now.

openers: Good news: it is far away and possibly a bad idea.
I would go myself but somebody has to hold the money.
caveats: Do not take the safe road, it is boring and longer anyway.
If you find something better on the way, tell me first.
signoffs: Go and see something!
Stories accepted in part payment.

openers: Now then. A small job, and eat something first.
Somebody has let this go too long, poor thing.
caveats: Do not go hungry, and do not go alone if you can help it.
Come back if it is too much. That is allowed.
signoffs: Take care of yourself out there.
There will be soup, and payment.

openers: I could do this properly. Where is the fun in that?
Whoever takes this is going to have an interesting afternoon.
caveats: I have not lied in this notice. I have merely arranged the truth attractively.
If it goes wrong, that is also a result.
signoffs: Do tell me how it goes. In detail.
No refunds, no regrets.

openers: Nobody else will do this, which is why it pays.
Let us skip the part where either of us pretends to care.
caveats: You will be blamed regardless. Get paid first.
Whatever they tell you out there, it is about money.
signoffs: Money, then goodbye.
Do not expect gratitude. Expect the fee.

openers: Task, scope, fee. In that order, no digressions.
Begin at first light. Finish before you are tired.
caveats: Follow the sequence exactly.
No shortcuts. Shortcuts are how records get broken badly.
signoffs: Standards, then payment.
Report on completion, not before.

openers: It will happen whether I post this or not. Still, here.
The job is already done somewhere. Kindly catch up.
caveats: Do not struggle against the details. They win.
If it ends badly it was always going to.
signoffs: What comes, comes.
The fee is certain. Little else is.

openers: Fine. Someone else can do it.
I have complained to everyone available. Now I am paying.
caveats: Do not chatter at me when you return. Just hand it over.
It will take longer than you think. Everything does.
signoffs: Hmph. Payment's payment.
Go on then.

openers: This is for people I owe, so I will owe you too.
A friend needs it. That is the whole reason.
caveats: Do not embarrass me out there.
If anyone asks, I vouched for you. Make that true.
signoffs: I do not forget favours.
You will have my word and my coin.

openers: Dangerous, honest work. My favourite advertisement.
I would take this myself if I were two people.
caveats: Do not run from the interesting part. Fight it or leave.
Fear is fine. Fleeing loses the fee.
signoffs: Stand up straight and go.
Come back with a scar and a story.

openers: I hope it is all right that I asked at all.
Only if you are not busy. Truly, only then.
caveats: If anyone shouts at you about it, blame me. It is fine.
Please do not take risks on my behalf.
signoffs: Thank you, if you do. And if not, that is fine too.
I will be over there. Waiting. Quietly.

openers: There is money in this and therefore wine after it.
Boring job, excellent fee, obvious conclusion.
caveats: Do not do it thirsty. Nothing good is done thirsty.
Finish before the evening. Evenings are for other work.
signoffs: First round is mine.
Come back and we will spend it properly.

openers: Someone should probably do this.
It is a job. I have no strong feelings.
caveats: Do it however. I genuinely do not mind.
If it does not get done, that is also an outcome.
signoffs: Whatever. Money's there.
Fine either way.

courier: {Carry|Escort|Move} this {parcel|consignment|case} to the quest board of [DEST]. {It is lighter than it looks.|Do not open it.|It ticks, but politely.|The contents are insured against everything except curiosity.}
One {package|bundle|tube} out of [HERE], one signature in [DEST]. {Nothing in between concerns you.|What happens between the two is your business and your risk.}

The {relay|regular runner|usual boy} is {ill|missing|drunk|three days overdue}, so the [DEST] board is waiting on a delivery nobody has made. {Take it there yourself.|Hand it over in person or not at all.}
{A small crate|A flat wooden box|A bound grimorie} must reach [DEST] {intact|unopened|by hand}. {We chose the road over the pigeons deliberately.|The pigeons refused this one.}
smuggle: A {crate|satchel|drum} needs to reach [DEST] without appearing on any manifest, grimorie or Archive publication. {Take the back roads.|If a checkpoint asks, it is pickled herring.|The seals are Fantablack, do not scratch them.}

Nothing illegal, {merely unregistered|merely unfiled|merely undocumented}. Get it to [DEST] and forget the weight. {Customs are counting crates this month.|The Archive is publishing manifests again, so keep off the highway.}
There is a {load|parcel|barrel} that must arrive in [DEST] without arriving officially. {Do not open it to find out why.|You are paid for the silence, not the distance.}

The {short road|highway|toll road} is watched. Take the {long way|old way|smugglers' way} into [DEST] with this and nobody has to file anything. {Checkpoints do not read pickled herring labels closely.}
supply: {We|The undersigned} will pay for [QTY]x [ITEM], delivered to any quest board. {Quality is negotiable, quantity is not.|No questions asked either way.|Weighed on honest scales.}
Our stock of [ITEM] {ran out|was stolen|never arrived|was requisitioned}. [QTY] units, any board, {cash on the table|payment on the spot}.
Buying [QTY]x [ITEM] at above the going rate {because we are desperate|because nobody else is selling|because the shipment sank}. {Bring them all at once, we are not doing this twice.}
[QTY]x [ITEM] wanted. {Sourced however you like.|We do not ask where materials come from, only whether they are dry.}
catering: The {kitchen|mess hall|feast committee} is short [QTY]x [ITEM] and the {banquet|wake|festival|shift change} will not wait. {Fresh preferred, edible required.|The last courier ate the cargo. Do not be the last courier.}
[QTY]x [ITEM], {before the guests arrive|before the pots go cold|by the second sitting}. {The cook is beyond reasoning with.|The cook has already thrown one pan.}
Forty mouths, one missing ingredient: [QTY]x [ITEM]. {Bring it and eat free.|Bring it and nobody has to know how close this came.}
A {wedding|wake|guild supper} has been planned for months and provisioned in an afternoon. We need [QTY]x [ITEM]. {Do not substitute. We will notice.}
procure: {Pay [COST] now|Advance [COST]} and a {crate|lot|consignment} of goods will be waiting for you at any quest board {within the day|once the roads clear|after the next pigeon}. {Stock is limited.|First come, first served.|References available on request.}
Investors of [COST] receive {one sealed lot|a full consignment} at any board, {shortly|in due course|as soon as the wagons come in}. {The margin is generous because the risk is ours.}
We are {liquidating|forwarding|clearing} stock: [COST] up front, goods collected later at any board. {Nobody has ever complained.|The paperwork is immaculate. Ask anyone.}
One payment of [COST] secures a {lot|shipment} that has not technically arrived yet. {The wagons exist.|The wagons are between here and elsewhere.}
donation: The [FACTION] relief fund accepts contributions of [COST] toward {blankets, boots and Anoki batteries|resettling refugees from the upper dimensions|keeping the soup cauldrons enchanted}. Donors are remembered.
[COST] to the [FACTION] {hardship box|winter fund|widows' list}. {No sum is too small, though yours could be larger.|Names of donors are read aloud, briefly.}
Give [COST] and [FACTION] will {feed someone|shelter someone|bury someone properly} this week. {The grimorie is public.|The receipt is worth more than the coin, in the right rooms.}
cache: A {cache|strongbox|supply drop} {went missing|was abandoned|was buried in a hurry} at coordinates ([X], [Y]). {Recover it and keep what is portable, the finder's fee covers the rest.|Bring back whatever the weather left.}
Somebody left a {box|bundle|case} at ([X], [Y]) and then stopped writing letters. {We would like the box.|We are not asking about the somebody.}
Coordinates ([X], [Y]). There is a container there {under canvas|under stones|under a dead tree}. {It is ours by paperwork if not by geography.|Ownership is arguable, possession is not.}
Our {drop|dead-letter box} at ([X], [Y]) has not been emptied in {weeks|a season|far too long}. {Go and empty it.|Whatever is in there is going stale.}
dig: {An excavation permit has been issued for|Old maps disagree about|A collapsed cellar has opened at} coordinates ([X], [Y]). Bring a shovel. {Whatever predates the Squishing belongs to history.|Handle the stratum gently.|If it hums, stop digging and start running.}
The ground at ([X], [Y]) is {softer than it should be|marked on a map nobody admits to drawing|giving up coins}. Dig it. {Bring a shovel, we have none to lend.}
A {barrow|foundation|spoil heap} at ([X], [Y]) needs opening {properly|carefully|before somebody less careful does it}. Shovel required. {Record the layers even if you cannot read them.}
There is {something|a floor|a lid} about a metre under ([X], [Y]). {We would like to know what.|Dig until it stops being soil.}
statues: Locate and scan [N] statues at coordinates ([X], [Y]). {The Foundation catalogues everything, including the embarrassing ones.|Rubbings are acceptable, memories are not.|Note any inscription verbatim.}
[N] {figures|effigies|carved stones} stand near ([X], [Y]) and none of them are in the register. {Fix that.|Approach each one and record it.}
Somebody carved [N] statues at ([X], [Y]) and told nobody. {We are the nobody, catching up.|Count them, describe them, leave them standing.}
signs: Walk the roads near ([X], [Y]) and verify [N] signposts against the registry. {Half the countryside is misdirected and the Truckers are furious.|A wrong sign near a loop bubble is manslaughter with extra steps.}
[N] signposts around ([X], [Y]) may or may not still say what they were built to say. {Check each one.|Trust the post, not the paint.}
Since the last storm the signs near ([X], [Y]) have been {creative|imaginative|unhelpful}. Verify [N] of them. {Report any that point at nothing.}
clearing: The ground at ([X], [Y]) must be cleared: remove [N] {trees, boulders or debris|obstacles} by hand. {Tools provided by you.|The petrodemon next door insists on quiet work.}
[N] {trunks|boulders|piles of rubble} are sitting where a road is supposed to go, at ([X], [Y]). {Move them.|Take them apart, we do not care how.}
Right of way at ([X], [Y]) is blocked {again|as usual|by whatever fell last week}. Clear [N] obstacles. {Firewood is yours to keep.}
bounty_criminal: {A warrant has been issued for|The judiciary of Eris seeks|A price now rests on} [ENEMY], {level [LVL], armed and talkative|a known face at level [LVL]}, last seen holding ground at ([X], [Y]). {Dead settles the account.|The court accepts no excuses, only results.}

[ENEMY] (Lv [LVL]) has been {robbing couriers|extorting the villages|running their own toll} out of ([X], [Y]) for {a season|a year|longer than anyone will admit}. {The warrant does not specify condition on delivery.}
We have tried {reasoning|paying|arresting} [ENEMY]. What remains is a bounty. Lv [LVL], at ([X], [Y]). {Bring proof, not stories.}
bounty_monster: {Something|A [ENEMY]} has {claimed|nested at|been dragging travellers toward} coordinates ([X], [Y]). {It does not negotiate.|It is not native to that ground, which worries the locals more.|Level [LVL]. Bring friends.}
A [ENEMY] of about level [LVL] is {denning|feeding|breeding} at ([X], [Y]). {Nobody grazes there any more.|The road past it is now a rumour.}
Whatever is at ([X], [Y]) was described by three witnesses as three different animals. Our register calls it [ENEMY], Lv [LVL]. {Kill it and settle the argument.}
survey: Walk the ground at coordinates ([X], [Y]) and come back in one piece. {That is the whole job.|Your presence there is the deliverable.|If the coordinates are gone, report that too.}
Stand at ([X], [Y]). {Look around. Leave.|That is all. Truly.|We need a witness, not a report.}
The maps say one thing about ([X], [Y]) and the last traveller said another. {Go and break the tie.|Somebody has to be there in person.}
survey_dest: Travel to [DEST] and see it with your own eyes. {Rumours travel faster than trucks, we need slower facts.|Any honest pair of boots qualifies.}
We have {three|four|five} contradictory reports out of [DEST] and no reason to believe any of them. {Go and look.|Arrive, observe, return.}
Somebody reliable in [DEST], briefly. {Then come back and say what you saw, in order.}
pilgrimage: Make the journey to [DEST] {as penance|as witness|for the record of the faithful}. {The road itself is the prayer.|Arrive humble, leave receipts.}
A {parishioner|brother|debtor} promised to walk to [DEST] and then {died|reconsidered|left the faith}. {The promise stands. Walk it for them.}
Reach [DEST] on foot if you can bear it. {The distance is the point.|Nobody checks how, but the road knows.}
interview: Find any citizen of [DEST] and {listen to them properly|record their words|empathize, in the technical sense}. {Publish-ready notes preferred.|The Foundation pays for voices, not opinions.}
One conversation in [DEST], conducted {honestly|patiently|without leading the witness}. {We pay for what they say, not what you think.}
Somebody in [DEST] knows something and does not know that they know it. {Talk to anybody. Start there.}
offworld: {A sample|A beacon payload|Something the Kessler cloud spared} waits on the surface of [PLANET], system [SYSTEM]. Land, recover the cache, {try to ignore the local weather|and mind the re-entry paperwork}.
There is a cache on [PLANET] ([SYSTEM]) that {predates our landing rights|nobody has been able to reach|two crews have already failed to collect}. {The third attempt is yours.}
Set down on [PLANET] in [SYSTEM] and bring back the sample container. {The atmosphere is survivable. Mostly.|Do not linger past nightfall, whatever nightfall means there.}
arena: A {sponsor|syndicate|retired gladiator with opinions} will pay for [N] {sanctioned|reasonably sanctioned} arena victories. {Win pretty if you can, win anyway if you cannot.|The crowd remembers names.}
[N] wins in the pit, {under any name you like|however you can get them}. {The bets are already placed.|Somebody has money on you and it is not us.}
We are building a reputation and would like to rent yours: [N] arena victories. {Losing is permitted, but unpaid.}
cull: The {roads|fields|approaches} are crawling. Put down [N] hostiles, {any species, any excuse|receipts in viscera}. {The count is on your honor and our informants.|Overachievement is not reimbursed.}
[N] {hostiles|things|nuisances}, anywhere, any manner. {We are past being particular.|The countryside is overstocked and we are underpaid.}
Piecework: [N] confirmed kills. {We are not asking what they were.|Nobody counts species any more, only heads.}
market: Acquire and hold [N] shares of crude oil. {The Collective files this under enthusiasm.|Sell afterwards if you like, we only need the grimorie entry.}
Hold [N] oil shares long enough for the grimorie to notice. {What you do with them afterwards is your affair.|The position matters, the profit is yours.}
Somebody needs the register to show [N] shares of crude in {friendly|private|unaffiliated} hands. {Yours will do.}
expedition: Reach coordinates ([X], [Y]), recover the cache waiting there, then report to the quest board of [DEST]. {Three legs, one contract.|The route is the easy part. Probably.}
Out to ([X], [Y]), collect, then in to [DEST]. {Do not shortcut the middle step, the box is the job.|One trip, three signatures.}
The cache at ([X], [Y]) belongs on a desk in [DEST]. {Carry it the whole way yourself.|Relays lose things, and we have lost enough.}
purge: Something at ([X], [Y]) is standing between us and a {vault|cache|stores room}. Kill it, then bring out what it was guarding. {In that order, please.}
There is a {guardian|squatter|tenant} at ([X], [Y]) with no lease and considerable teeth. {Evict it, then empty the store behind it.}
Our property at ([X], [Y]) is currently inhabited. {Deal with the inhabitant. Then collect.|We want the contents. The occupant is an obstacle, not a negotiation.}
grand_tour: Ride the circuit: present yourself at each listed settlement, in any order. {The Society keeps its maps honest with boots like yours.|Stamp your card at every board.}
Show your face at every stop on the list. {Order does not matter, attendance does.|We are checking that the roads between them still exist.}
A full round of the settlements below, {at your own pace|in whatever order the weather allows}. {Each arrival counts once.}
elite_hunt: SUBJECT: [ENEMY]. ASSESSED LEVEL: [LVL]. LOCATION: ([X], [Y]), and it has not moved in {weeks|months|as long as anyone has been counting}. It arrived {without warning|during the storms|the week the road closed|from a direction that does not have a road} and settled onto the site as though it had been promised it. {Livestock went first, then the outbuildings, then the people who went to look at the outbuildings.|Everything within a mile has either left or stopped moving.|Three families abandoned holdings they had farmed for four generations rather than share a valley with it.} What we know is thin and expensive: {it does not sleep|it does not bleed the way things bleed|it hears intent before it hears footsteps|it is patient, which is the worst of it}, and {every ranged attempt has been wasted|it closes distance faster than the reports suggested|armour has made no measurable difference}. The job is to kill it. {There is no secondary objective, no sample to bring back, no report to file.|Nothing else about the site matters and nothing else will be paid for.} {The fee is what it is because the arithmetic is what it is.|The sum below has been raised twice and taken zero times.}

This contract has been open since {the spring|last winter|before the current clerk was hired} and we have stopped pretending it is routine. The target is [ENEMY], level [LVL], holding ground at ([X], [Y]). {Four|Five|Six|Seven} parties have accepted it before you. {None of them came back.|Two came back, neither whole, neither talkative.|One came back alone and has not spoken since.} From what those returns told us: {it fights in the open by choice|it does not defend a lair, it defends a radius|it is stronger after dark, or believes it is, which amounts to the same thing|it will let you approach, which is not mercy}. {Bring everything.|Bring your best, and bring more of it than you think reasonable.|Bring a party, not a plan.} {We pay on proof, and proof is its absence from that coordinate.|Payment is immediate, in full, and frankly a relief to be rid of.} {If you decide against it, take the notice down and let somebody braver read the board.|If you read this and walk away, nobody here will think less of you.}

A formal threat assessment was completed on [ENEMY] at ([X], [Y]) and the conclusion was that no force we can field is adequate. Assessed level: [LVL]. {The assessment took eleven days. Nine of them were spent arguing about the number.|The assessor asked to be reassigned on completion and was.} Behaviourally: {it does not roam, it accretes|it collects the remains of what it kills and arranges them|it responds to noise, to light, and to being discussed nearby|it appears to be waiting for something specific}. Structurally: {conventional weapons have been tried and logged as ineffective|it has survived fire, water and a controlled collapse|two of its wounds from last season have closed}. The contract is a kill order and nothing else. {Do not attempt capture.|Do not attempt communication, whatever it appears to offer.|Do not bring anything you would mind losing, including people.} {The fee reflects the assessment rather than the effort.|We are paying for a result nobody has produced yet.}

Read the whole notice before you decide, because the short version has already killed people. [ENEMY], level [LVL], at ([X], [Y]). {It has been there long enough that the maps have been redrawn around it.|The road past that coordinate is now marked impassable, which is a polite way of putting it.|Two settlements have quietly rerouted their entire year around not going near it.} {Nobody knows where it came from and everybody has a theory.|The theories are worthless. The body count is not.} Practical detail, such as we have: {approach from the open ground, not the treeline|do not split up, it counts|it is slow to start and impossible to stop|whatever it does first is not what it does second}. {Kill it and the coordinate goes back to being a field.|End it and half this district can go home.} {The money has been set aside for a year and grows no smaller for waiting.|The purse is sealed and witnessed. It is yours the hour it dies.}
pet: We want a [ENEMY], Lv [LVL], {alive|breathing|unbroken} and willing to follow somebody home. {Talk it round, do not beat it down.|Killing one is easy and pays nothing here.} Hand it over at any board and it becomes ours.

There is a [ENEMY] out there that could be persuaded to be {a companion|a mascot|somebody's pet} instead of a problem. {Persuade it.|That is the entire job: make a friend, then give the friend away.} Deliver it at any board.

Bring in one tame [ENEMY]. {We are told it can be done with patience and the right tone of voice.|Talk first. Fight only if talking is clearly over.} It stops being yours the moment you collect the fee.
A living [ENEMY] (Lv [LVL]) is wanted as {a companion|a curiosity|a working animal}. {Tame it, walk it in, sign it over.|No cages, no wounds, no substitutions.}
research: First scan the statues at ([X], [Y]), then interview a citizen of [DEST] about what you saw. {Method matters: stones first, people second.|The monograph will credit you in a footnote.}
Two sources, one paper: the stones at ([X], [Y]) and a living voice in [DEST]. {In that order, or the argument collapses.}
Record the monuments at ([X], [Y]), then ask somebody in [DEST] what their grandmother called them. {The discrepancy is the finding.}
